Thanks for the context — quick technical bullets below (I also attached a one-pager summarizing tradeoffs).

Batching recommendations:
- Low latency interactive use (median p95 <200ms): keep batch sizes <= 8 and prefer per-request concurrency over large batching; incremental batching helps but avoid cross-session batching for auth-sensitive data.
- Throughput-heavy background workloads (embeddings / reranking): batch sizes 32–256 give 2–4x throughput improvements depending on sequence length and model quant.
- Auto-batching policy: we recommend adaptive batching with a 30–80ms hold window; this balances tail latency with utilization.

Caching guidance:
- KV/prefix cache: effective when users have repeat prompts or system-prefilled context; expect 20–60% token savings on chat-style workloads with stable context.
- Cache invalidation: TTLs of 6–24 hours for session templates; use explicit invalidation for user profile updates.

Quantization recommendations:
- int8 (symmetric) on large models: good for non-safety-critical generation (roughly 1–3% measured ROUGE/semantic drift on our evals); reduces cost ~30–40% depending on hardware.
- mixed-precision (int8 weights + fp16 activations): best quality/cost tradeoff for LLMs with moderate latency impact.
- For safety/content-sensitive outputs (financial compliance): avoid aggressive quantization for the final ranker; run regressions on a small labeled set before rollout.

Operational notes for packaging/pricing:
- If TideBank plans to use a dedicated pool (reserved GPUs), we can include a quantization qualification phase at no extra charge during the first month.
- We recommend a small fraud/regression prompt set (50–200 prompts) to validate any quant profile before committing.

Attached: quant-reco-one-pager.pdf
